comparisons.peer_topic: Specific Regulatory Actions, Settlements, and Misconduct Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Regulators possess broad supervisory authority and enforcement powers, leading to significant compliance costs from settlements and consent orders, such as the December 2024 OCC Consent Order against BANA and settlements regarding Zelle payments, uninvested cash rates, and credit card marketing. Failure to meet regulatory requirements or maintain adequate risk controls can result in further fines, penalties, and restrictions. Additionally, employee misconduct, whether actual or perceived, including ethical violations, conflicts of interest, or fraud, exposes the company to litigation, government enforcement actions, and reputational harm, often resulting in overlapping investigations by multiple jurisdictions.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose the risk of significant regulatory intervention and enforcement actions due to their status in the financial services industry. GS highlights its specific classification as a systemically important financial institution subject to extensive global regulation and risk of intervention by taxing authorities. BAC similarly notes regulators' broad prudential and supervisory authority, but explicitly cites specific recent enforcement outcomes (e.g., December 2024 OCC Consent Order) and detailed regulatory focus areas like anti-money laundering and economic sanctions, whereas GS focuses on the general risk of overlapping and divergent regulations across jurisdictions.

sentences.text: As a participant in the financial services industry and a systemically important financial institution, we are subject to extensive regulation in jurisdictions around the world.
We face the risk of significant intervention by law enforcement, regulatory and taxing authorities, as well as private litigation, in all jurisdictions in which we conduct our businesses.

Our regulators' prudential and supervisory authority gives them broad power and discretion to direct our actions, and they have assumed an active oversight, inspection and investigatory role across the financial services industry.

As part of their enforcement authority, our regulators and other government authorities have the authority to, among other things, conduct investigations and assess significant civil or criminal monetary fines, penalties or restitution, issue cease and desist orders, suspend or withdraw licenses and authorizations, initiate injunctive action, apply regulatory sanctions or cause us to enter into consent orders.

comparisons.peer_topic: Challenging regulatory environment and investigation complexity
comparisons.peer_summary: The challenging global judicial and regulatory environment means a single issue may trigger numerous overlapping investigations by multiple agencies in the U.S. and abroad, as well as civil litigation, diverting management attention and increasing costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi emphasize the complexity and global scope of regulatory scrutiny, particularly the risk of overlapping investigations. GS states that its activities are subject to 'overlapping and divergent regulation in different jurisdictions.' Citi provides a more granular explanation, noting that a single event may give rise to 'a large number of overlapping investigations and regulatory proceedings... by multiple federal and state agencies... or by multiple regulators... in foreign jurisdictions.' Both identify this complexity as a source of diverted management attention and increased costs.

sentences.text: In many cases, our activities have been and may continue to be subject to overlapping and divergent regulation in different jurisdictions.

The complexity of the federal and state regulatory and enforcement regimes in the U.S., coupled with the global scope of Citi's operations, also means that a single event or issue may give rise to a large number of overlapping investigations and regulatory proceedings, either by multiple federal and state agencies and authorities in the U.S. or by multiple regulators and other governmental entities in foreign jurisdictions, as well as multiple civil litigation claims in multiple jurisdictions.
Responding to regulatory inquiries and proceedings can be time consuming and costly, and divert management attention from Citi's businesses.

comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorganChase faces significant legal risks from ongoing litigation, class actions, derivative actions, and criminal proceedings, as well as formal and informal regulatory and government investigations. These matters could result in adverse judgments, settlements, fines, penalties, or sanctions that may materially and adversely affect the company's business, financial condition, results of operations, or reputation. As a financial services participant, the company expects to continue experiencing a high level of such legal and regulatory scrutiny.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorganChase explicitly link their regulatory risk exposure to their participation in the financial services industry, with JPMorganChase extending this to include a 'high level of litigation.' GS warns of 'significant intervention by law enforcement, regulatory and taxing authorities, as well as private litigation.' JPMorganChase similarly identifies 'significant legal risks from litigation and formal and informal regulatory and government investigations' and notes that other institutions' violations often trigger investigations of JPMorganChase as well, highlighting a shared ecosystem risk.

sentences.text: We face the risk of significant intervention by law enforcement, regulatory and taxing authorities, as well as private litigation, in all jurisdictions in which we conduct our businesses.
JPMorganChase faces significant legal risks from litigation and formal and informal regulatory and government investigations.

In addition, if another financial institution violates a law or regulation relating to a particular business activity or practice, this will often give rise to an investigation by regulators and other governmental agencies of the same or similar activity or practice by JPMorganChase.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory and Legal Enforcement Risk Outcomes
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm faces extensive litigation and regulatory investigations globally, which may result in adverse judgments, fines, penalties, and collateral consequences such as business limitations, as well as requirements to undertake specific measures to resolve proceedings.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley disclose the broad geographic and regulatory scope of potential enforcement actions. GS states it faces risks in 'all jurisdictions in which we conduct our businesses.' Morgan Stanley echoes this by stating it faces the 'risk of investigations and proceedings by governmental and self-regulatory organizations in all countries in which we conduct our business.' Both also highlight that these actions can result in significant fines, penalties, and adverse judgments, with MS specifically listing 'disgorgement, restitution, forfeiture, injunctions' as potential outcomes alongside the general reputational and financial damage cited by both.

sentences.text: We face the risk of significant intervention by law enforcement, regulatory and taxing authorities, as well as private litigation, in all jurisdictions in which we conduct our businesses.
As a global financial services firm, we face the risk of investigations and proceedings by governmental and self-regulatory organizations in all countries in which we conduct our business.

Investigations and proceedings initiated by these authorities may result in adverse judgments, settlements, fines, penalties, disgorgement, restitution, forfeiture, injunctions or other relief, and have included and may in the future include requirements that the Firm admit certain conduct, which may result in increased exposure to civil litigation.
